hints: Look at the force triangle in the diagram: $P$ is adjacent to the angle $\theta$, while $F$ is the hypotenuse.
Connect this to the component rule $P = F\cos\theta$ for fixed magnitude $F$ and check the two ends $\theta = 0^{\circ}$ and $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.
Think how $\cos\theta$ changes: its gradient is zero near $0^{\circ}$ and steepest near $90^{\circ}$, so decide which decreasing $P$ against $\theta$ curve has a flat top and steep finish.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: $F$ has fixed magnitude and $P$ is the horizontal projection adjacent to angle $\theta$ in the diagram.
State the component rule: adjacent component equals hypotenuse times cosine, so $P = F\cos\theta$.
Check the end points: at $\theta = 0^{\circ}$, $\cos 0^{\circ} = 1$ so $P = F$ is maximum; at $\theta = 90^{\circ}$, $\cos 90^{\circ} = 0$ so $P = 0$.
Check the shape between: $\cos\theta$ falls slowly at first where its slope is near zero, then falls more steeply toward $90^{\circ}$, giving a curve that is flat-topped then curves down to zero.
Match this to the graphs: only the decreasing curve starting at maximum $P$, flat at $\theta = 0$ and steepest as it reaches zero at $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ fits. This is option A.

A.explanation: P equals $F\cos\theta$, which is maximum at $0^{\circ}$ and zero at $90^{\circ}$ with a cosine curve that is flat at the start.

B.explanation: This shows $P$ increasing from zero, which would be the vertical component $F\sin\theta$, not the adjacent horizontal component.

C.explanation: This shows $P$ starting at zero and increasing, which contradicts $P=F$ when $\theta=0^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: This decreases to zero but has the wrong curvature - steep at $0^{\circ}$ and flat at $90^{\circ}$ - opposite to $\cos\theta$.
